subject_entity.notes: Gnostic teacher active in Alexandria under Hadrian and Antoninus Pius (c. 117–145). Taught that the supreme God (Abraxas) was unknowable; 365 heavens; the God of the Jews was the lowest angel. Infamously denied that Christ suffered — teaching that Simon of Cyrene was crucified in his place while Jesus stood by and laughed.

object_entity.proposition_label: Christ truly became flesh and truly suffered in the body
object_entity.description: The incarnate Christ was a genuine human being who truly was born, truly suffered, truly died, and truly rose again; not a phantom or appearance as the Docetists claimed.

evidence.notes: A Christ who swapped forms with Simon and only appeared to be crucified did not truly become flesh.

passage.excerpt: Basilides says that there is one unbegotten father, by name Abraxas, by whom was born Nous; from Nous, Logos; from Logos, Phronesis; from Phronesis, Sophia and Dynamis; and from these the rulers, angels, and first heaven. He affirmed that Jesus did not suffer death, but that Simon of Cyrene was compelled to carry his cross for him, and was crucified in his stead — transfigured so as to appear to be Jesus. But Jesus himself received the form of Simon and, standing by, laughed at those who crucified him.

evidence.notes: Eusebius HE 4.7.2 places Basilides at Alexandria under Hadrian.

passage.excerpt: At the time of the Emperor Hadrian the heresiarchs arose to plague the Church. Saturninus came from Antioch and Basilides from Alexandria. From that time the so-called Gnostic heresy spread like a pestilence. Basilides feigned loftier mysteries and procured the downfall of many in Alexandria; he taught that Christ had not truly suffered but that Simon of Cyrene was substituted and crucified. Saturninus taught that the Saviour was unborn and bodiless, appearing only in the semblance of a man.
